title: St. Augustine, Florida
excerpt: A charter bus to St. Augustine handles what the old city cannot: narrow streets and scarce parking. Where to drop off, what to see, which vehicle fits.

extraImage.alt: A tour group stepping down from a mini bus at the edge of the historic district in St. Augustine on a clear morning

body.text: St. Augustine is the oldest continuously inhabited European-established settlement in the United States, founded in 1565, and it wears that history in a way few American cities can. It is also, for exactly the same reason, a difficult place to bring a group in private cars. A charter bus to St. Augustine solves a problem the city itself creates: streets laid out in the sixteenth century, a historic core best seen on foot, and parking that fills early and stays full.

Get the vehicle question right and St. Augustine is one of the easiest group destinations in Florida. Get it wrong and your group spends the first hour of the day circling for spaces in four separate cars.
The parking problem, and how to sidestep it

The historic district is compact, roughly a dozen walkable blocks, and that is its great strength. St. George Street, the spine of the old town, is pedestrian-only. Cars cannot use it and neither can coaches. The surrounding streets are narrow, often one-way, and lined with buildings that have stood for centuries and are not going to move for your bus.

The practical answer is the same one that works in Key West. Treat the vehicle as a shuttle rather than a follower. Your driver sets the group down at an agreed point on the edge of the district, the group explores on foot, and the vehicle collects everyone at a fixed time and place. Because the old town is so small, nobody walks far. Groups that plan this way consistently report it as the smoothest part of their trip, while groups that arrive without a plan lose the morning.
What to build the day around

items: Castillo de San Marcos, the coquina fortress on Matanzas Bay completed in 1695 and never taken by force. It is a National Monument and the single strongest anchor for a group visit. Allow ninety minutes.
St. George Street for the shops, the Colonial Quarter and the old schoolhouse. Pedestrian-only, so it absorbs a large group comfortably.
The Lightner Museum, housed in Henry Flagler's former Alcazar Hotel, with a Gilded Age collection that surprises people who came only for the Spanish history.
Flagler College, whose former Ponce de Leon Hotel building has Tiffany stained glass and offers tours. Excellent for adult and student groups alike.
The St. Augustine Lighthouse across the bay on Anastasia Island, with 219 steps and a genuinely good view for anyone who climbs them.
Nights of Lights, running from November into January, when the historic district is lit throughout. It is spectacular and it is the busiest the city gets.

body.text: Why a charter bus to St. Augustine works so well

Beyond parking, the reason groups keep choosing a coach here is that St. Augustine pairs naturally with other stops. Jacksonville is about forty minutes north. Daytona Beach is roughly an hour south. Orlando is around two hours southwest. A chartered vehicle turns those from separate trips into one itinerary, and it means your group can add a beach afternoon on Anastasia Island without anybody rearranging cars.

It also keeps the group together, which matters more in a walkable historic city than people expect. Everyone arrives at once, everyone leaves at once, and the day does not fragment into four groups on four schedules.
Matching the vehicle to the group

items: For 40 or more, a coach from our [motor coach fleet](/fleet/motor-coaches) carries the group in comfort on the highway legs from Jacksonville, Orlando or further afield, with luggage space underneath for a multi-day itinerary.

For 20 to 32, a [mini bus](/fleet/mini-buses) is the practical choice for St. Augustine specifically. It is far easier to position near the historic district and simpler on the narrow approach streets.
For smaller groups of 10 to 14, a [sprinter van](/fleet/sprinter-vans) can get closer to the old town than anything larger and is ideal for a leadership retreat or an extended family.
For school and youth groups, a [school bus](/fleet/school-buses) seating 28 to 60 is usually the most economical option for a day trip from elsewhere in North Florida.

body.text: Autumn and spring are the best months here. October through April brings comfortable temperatures and lower humidity, which matters a great deal in a destination where the whole point is walking outdoors. Summer is hot and humid with frequent afternoon storms, and the historic district offers limited shade. Hurricane season runs from June through November, and St. Augustine's low-lying waterfront has seen flooding in past storms, so September and October itineraries benefit from flexible arrangements.
If your group wants Nights of Lights, book early. It is the city's peak season and both accommodation and coach availability tighten considerably from mid-November onward.

items: Agree the drop-off and collection point with your coordinator in advance, and tell the whole group the collection time twice.
The historic district rewards comfortable shoes. Much of it is uneven brick and coquina.
Castillo de San Marcos is federally run and its hours differ from the shops around it. Check them when you build the schedule.
Consider a guided walking tour for the first hour. It orients a large group quickly and reduces the number of people who get lost later.
